ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, there is a circle with G as the center, and A, C, D, F are all on the circle; DF is a chord, and point E is on chord DF; the line segment GE from the center G to chord DF is labeled as 10, indicating the perpendicular distance from the center of the circle to this chord. The problem gives the radius of the circle as 26, so D being on the circle means GD = 26. Then reason: the perpendicular line from the center of a circle to a chord bisects that chord, so E is the midpoint of DF, and GE is perpendicular to DF, so triangle GED is a right triangle. By the Pythagorean theorem, DE^2 + GE^2 = GD^2, so DE = sqrt(26^2 - 10^2) = sqrt(676 - 100) = sqrt(576) = 24.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as circle centered at G, with D and F on the circle and chord DF containing point E. The segment GE from the center to chord DF is marked 10 and represents the perpendicular distance from the center to that chord. Since D is on the circle, GD is a radius, so GD = 26 from the text. Use the theorem that the perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord, so E is the midpoint of DF and triangle GED is right. Then compute DE from the right triangle using DE^2 + GE^2 = GD^2, giving DE = sqrt(26^2 - 10^2) = 24.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing two chords, AC and DF, with center-to-chord distances GB and GE both marked 10, and radius 26. Work first with chord AC: since B is the foot from the center to chord AC, triangle GBA is right with GA = 26 and GB = 10, so AB = sqrt(26^2 - 10^2) = 24. Thus AC = 48 because the perpendicular from the center bisects the chord. Then use the given text statement that chords AC and DF are equidistant from the center, so the chords are congruent: DF = AC = 48. Since GE is perpendicular from the center to DF, it bisects DF, so DE = DF/2 = 24.
